mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% in a single month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over a 3-month period indicates growing demand and economic expansion, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer confidence and spending rise.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where HOUST shows a sustained increase, or if the correlation between HOUST growth and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% over a 3-month period signals a tightening labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings improve due to increased economic activity.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the correlation between UNRATE decreases and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in industrial production (INDPRO) over a 3-month period indicates growing supply-side activity, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as increased production boosts corporate earnings.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where INDPRO shows a sustained increase, or if the correlation between INDPRO growth and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) grow faster than GDP (GDPC1) over a 3-month period, it signals a shift towards consumer-driven growth, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending boosts corporate earnings.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS growth > GDPC1 growth in 3 months
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the interaction between RSAFS and GDPC1 growth and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) and decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) over a 3-month period signals a strengthening labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as increased employment boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases & UNRATE decreases in 3 months
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the interaction between PAYEMS increase and UNRATE decrease and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) over a 3-month period, coupled with a federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 2%, signals inflationary pressure without corresponding monetary tightening, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate further monetary easing.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the interaction between CPIAUCSL increase and low FEDFUNDS and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) coupled with an increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over a 3-month period signals deflationary consumer-driven growth, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as deflationary pressures weigh on corporate earnings.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL decreases & RSAFS increases in 3 months
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the interaction between CPIAUCSL decrease and RSAFS increase and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
